text: Sir Thomas More, son of Sir John More, a justice of the King’s Bench, was born in 1478, in Milk Street, in the city of London.
zh: 托马斯·莫尔爵士 (Sir Thomas More) 是国王法官约翰·莫尔爵士 (Sir John More) 的儿子，1478 年出生于伦敦市米尔克街。
chunks: Sir Thomas More,
son of Sir John More,
a justice of the King’s Bench,
was born in 1478, in Milk Street,
in the city of London.

text: Archbishop of Canterbury and Lord Chancellor.
zh: 坎特伯雷大主教兼大法官。
chunks: Archbishop of Canterbury
and Lord Chancellor.

text: It was not unusual for persons of wealth or influence and sons of good families to be so established together in a relation of patron and client.
zh: 对于有钱有势的人和出身名门的人来说，建立起赞助人与受托人的关系并不罕见。
chunks: It was not unusual for persons of wealth
or influence and sons
of good families to be
so established together in a relation
of patron and client.

text: The youth wore his patron’s livery, and added to his state.

chunks: The youth wore his patron’s livery,
and added
to his state.

chunks: The patron used, afterwards,
his wealth
or influence
in helping his young client forward
in the world.

text: He once said, “Whoever shall live to try it, shall see this child here waiting at table prove a notable and rare man.
zh: 他曾经说过：“无论谁有生之年尝试一下，都会看到这个在餐桌旁等候的孩子是一位著名的、罕见的人。
chunks: He once said, “Whoever shall live
to try it,
shall see this child here waiting
at table prove a notable
and rare man.

text: Linacre, a physician, who afterwards took orders, was also the founder of the College of Physicians.
zh: 利纳克尔是一位医生，后来奉命行事，也是医师学院的创始人。
chunks: Linacre, a physician,
who afterwards took orders,
was also the founder
of the College
of Physicians.

text: More’s earnest character caused him while studying law to aim at the subduing of the flesh, by wearing a hair shirt, taking a log for a pillow, and whipping himself on Fridays.
zh: 莫尔的认真性格使他在学习法律时就以征服肉体为目标，穿着毛衬衫，用木头当枕头，每周五鞭打自己。
chunks: More’s earnest character caused him while studying law to aim
at the subduing of the flesh,
by wearing a hair shirt,
taking a log for a pillow,
and whipping himself on Fridays.

text: At the age of twenty-one he entered Parliament, and soon after he had been called to the bar he was made Under-Sheriff of London.
zh: 二十一岁时，他进入议会，获得律师资格后不久，他就被任命为伦敦副警长。
chunks: At the age
of twenty-one he entered Parliament,
and soon after he had been called
to the bar he was made Under-Sheriff
of London.

text: Commons Henry VII.’s proposal for a subsidy on account of the marriage portion of his daughter Margaret; and he opposed with so much energy that the House refused to grant it.
zh: 下议院亨利七世因其女儿玛格丽特的婚姻部分而提出的补贴提案；他强烈反对，以致众议院拒绝批准。
chunks: Commons Henry VII.’s proposal for a subsidy on account
of the marriage portion
of his daughter Margaret; and he opposed
with so much energy
that the House refused to grant it.

text: One went and told the king that a beardless boy had disappointed all his expectations.
zh: 其中一个人去告诉国王，一个没有胡子的男孩辜负了他的所有期望。
chunks: One went
and told the king that a beardless boy had disappointed all his expectations.

text: During the last years, therefore, of Henry VII.
zh: 因此，在亨利七世的最后几年。
chunks: During the last years, therefore,
of Henry VII.

text: More was under the displeasure of the king, and had thoughts of leaving the country.
zh: 莫尔因国王不满，萌生了出国的念头。
chunks: More was
under the displeasure
of the king,
and had thoughts
of leaving the country.

text: Henry VII. died in April, 1509, when More’s age was a little over thirty.
chunks: Henry VII. died
in April, 1509,
when More’s age was a little
over thirty.

text: In the first years of the reign of Henry VIII. he rose to large practice in the law courts, where it is said he refused to plead in cases which he thought unjust, and took no fees from widows, orphans, or the poor.
zh: 在亨利八世统治的最初几年。他在法庭上的地位很高，据说他拒绝为他认为不公正的案件辩护，并且不向寡妇、孤儿或穷人收取任何费用。
chunks: In the first years of the reign of Henry VIII. he rose
to large practice in the law courts,
where it is said he refused
to plead in cases which he thought unjust,
and took no fees from widows, orphans, or the poor.

text: John Colt, of New Hall, in Essex, but chose her elder sister, that he might not subject her to the discredit of being passed over.
zh: 来自埃塞克斯郡纽霍尔的约翰·柯尔特却选择了她的姐姐，以免她因被忽视而蒙受耻辱。
chunks: John Colt, of New Hall, in Essex,
but chose her elder sister,
that he might not subject her
to the discredit
of being passed over.

text: In 1513 Thomas More, still Under-Sheriff of London, is said to have written his “History of the Life and Death of King Edward V., and of the Usurpation of Richard III.
zh: 1513 年，托马斯·莫尔（Thomas More），当时还是伦敦副警长，据说写下了《爱德华五世国王的生死史和理查三世的篡位史》。
chunks: In 1513 Thomas More,
still Under-Sheriff of London, is said
to have written his “History
of the Life and Death of King Edward V.,
and of the Usurpation of Richard III.

text: The book, which seems to contain the knowledge and opinions of More’s patron, Morton, was not printed until 1557, when its writer had been twenty-two years dead.
zh: 这本书似乎包含了莫尔的赞助人莫顿的知识和观点，直到 1557 年才出版，当时作者已去世 22 年。
chunks: The book, which seems
to contain the knowledge and opinions
of More’s patron, Morton,
was not printed until 1557,
when its writer had been twenty-two years dead.

text: It was then printed from a MS. in More’s handwriting.
zh: 然后从 MS 打印它。莫尔的笔迹。
chunks: It was then printed
from a MS. in More’s handwriting.

text: X.; Henry VIII. made him Lord Chancellor, and from that year until 1523 the King and the Cardinal ruled England with absolute authority, and called no parliament.
zh: X.;亨利八世。任命他为大法官，从那一年到 1523 年，国王和红衣主教以绝对权威统治英格兰，并且不召集议会。
chunks: X.; Henry VIII. made him Lord Chancellor,
and from that year
until 1523 the King
and the Cardinal ruled England
with absolute authority, and called no parliament.

text: Tunstal and others to confer with the ambassadors of Charles V., then only Archduke of Austria, upon a renewal of alliance.
zh: 通斯塔尔等人与查理五世（当时只有奥地利大公）的大使商议续订联盟事宜。
chunks: Tunstal and others to confer
with the ambassadors
of Charles V.,
then only Archduke of Austria,
upon a renewal of alliance.

text: More, aged about thirty-seven, was absent from England for six months, and while at Antwerp he established friendship with Peter Giles (Latinised Ægidius), a scholarly and courteous young man, who was secretary to the municipality of Antwerp.
chunks: More, aged about thirty-seven, was absent from England
for six months, and while at Antwerp he established friendship
with Peter Giles (Latinised Ægidius),
a scholarly and courteous young man,
who was secretary to the municipality of Antwerp.

text: Cuthbert Tunstal was a rising churchman, chancellor to the Archbishop of Canterbury, who in that year (1515) was made Archdeacon of Chester, and in May of the next year (1516) Master of the Rolls.
zh: 卡斯伯特·通斯塔尔 (Cuthbert Tunstal) 是一位冉冉升起的牧师，坎特伯雷大主教的大臣，同年（1515 年）被任命为切斯特大执事，并于次年（1516 年）5 月被任命为主教。
chunks: Cuthbert Tunstal was a rising churchman,
chancellor to the Archbishop of Canterbury, who in
that year (1515) was made Archdeacon
of Chester, and in May
of the next year (1516) Master of the Rolls.

text: Brussels, where they were in close companionship with Erasmus.
zh: 布鲁塞尔，他们与伊拉斯谟有着密切的友谊。
chunks: Brussels,
where they were
in close companionship
with Erasmus.

text: More’s “Utopia” was written in Latin, and is in two parts, of which the second, describing the place οὐτοπία—or Nusquama, as he called it sometimes in his letters—“Nowhere”), was probably written towards the close of 1515; the first part, introductory, early in 1516.
chunks: More’s “Utopia” was written in Latin, and is in two parts,

the first part, introductory, early in 1516.

text: Erasmus, Peter Giles, and other of More’s friends in Flanders.
zh: 伊拉斯谟、彼得·吉尔斯和莫尔在佛兰德斯的其他朋友。
chunks: Erasmus,
Peter Giles,
and other
of More’s friends
in Flanders.

text: It was then revised by More, and printed by Frobenius at Basle in November, 1518.
zh: 随后莫尔对其进行了修订，并于 1518 年 11 月由弗罗贝尼乌斯在巴塞尔印刷。
chunks: It was then revised
by More, and printed
by Frobenius
at Basle
in November, 1518.

text: Lord William Russell, attended his execution, vindicated his memory, and been spitefully deprived by James II. of his lectureship at St.
zh: 威廉·罗素勋爵出席了他的行刑，证明了他的记忆，但被詹姆斯二世恶意剥夺了。
chunks: Lord William Russell, attended his execution,
vindicated his memory,
and been spitefully deprived
by James II.
of his lectureship at St.

text: Burnet was drawn to the translation of “Utopia” by the same sense of unreason in high places that caused More to write the book.
chunks: Burnet was drawn
to the translation of “Utopia”
by the same sense
of unreason in high places
that caused More to write the book.

text: Burnet’s is the translation given in this volume.
zh: 伯内特的译本是本卷中给出的。
chunks: Burnet’s is the translation given
in this volume.

text: The name of the book has given an adjective to our language—we call an impracticable scheme Utopian.
zh: 这本书的名字给我们的语言起了一个形容词——我们把不切实际的计划称为乌托邦。
chunks: The name
of the book has given an adjective
to our language—
we call an impracticable scheme Utopian.

text: Yet, under the veil of a playful fiction, the talk is intensely earnest, and abounds in practical suggestion.
chunks: Yet, under the veil
of a playful fiction,
the talk is intensely earnest,
and abounds
in practical suggestion.

text: It is the work of a scholarly and witty Englishman, who attacks in his own way the chief political and social evils of his time.
zh: 这是一位博学而机智的英国人的作品，他以自己的方式攻击了他那个时代的主要政治和社会罪恶。
chunks: It is the work
of a scholarly
and witty Englishman, who attacks
in his own way the chief political
and social evils of his time.

text: Designedly fantastic in suggestion of details, “Utopia” is the work of a scholar who had read Plato’s “Republic,” and had his fancy quickened after reading Plutarch’s account of Spartan life under Lycurgus.
zh: 《乌托邦》在细节暗示方面精心设计，是一位学者的作品，他读过柏拉图的《理想国》，并在阅读普鲁塔克对莱库格斯统治下的斯巴达生活的描述后，他的想象力加速了。
chunks: Designedly fantastic in suggestion of details,
“Utopia” is the work of a scholar
who had read Plato’s “Republic,
” and had his fancy quickened after reading Plutarch’s account
of Spartan life under Lycurgus.

text: Beneath the veil of an ideal communism, into which there has been worked some witty extravagance, there lies a noble English argument.
zh: 在理想共产主义的面纱之下，有一些诙谐的夸张，隐藏着一种高贵的英国论点。
chunks: Beneath the veil
of an ideal communism,
into which there has been worked some witty extravagance,
there lies a noble English argument.

text: Sometimes More puts the case as of France when he means England.
zh: 有时，当莫尔指的是英格兰时，他会以法国为例。
chunks: Sometimes More puts the case
as of France when he means England.

text: Sometimes there is ironical praise of the good faith of Christian kings, saving the book from censure as a political attack on the policy of Henry VIII.
zh: 有时会对基督教国王的善意进行讽刺性的赞扬，使这本书免遭谴责，被认为是对亨利八世政策的政治攻击。
chunks: Sometimes there is ironical praise
of the good faith of Christian kings,
saving the book from censure
as a political attack
on the policy of Henry VIII.

text: Erasmus wrote to a friend in 1517 that he should send for More’s “Utopia,” if he had not read it, and “wished to see the true source of all political evils.
zh: 1517 年，伊拉斯谟写信给一位朋友，如果他还没有读过莫尔的《乌托邦》，他应该派人去取来，并且“希望看到所有政治罪恶的真正根源。
chunks: Erasmus wrote to a friend
in 1517 that he should send for More’s “Utopia,
” if he had not read it,
and “wished to see the true source
of all political evils.

text: A burgomaster of Antwerp is so pleased with it that he knows it all by heart.
zh: 安特卫普的一位市长对此非常满意，他将这一切都熟记于心。
chunks: A burgomaster
of Antwerp is so pleased with it that he knows it all by heart.

text: Henry VIII., the unconquered King of England, a prince adorned with all the virtues that become a great monarch, having some differences of no small consequence with Charles the most serene Prince of Castile, sent me into Flanders, as his ambassador, for treating and composing matters between them.
chunks: Henry VIII., the unconquered King of England, a prince adorned with all the virtues
that become a great monarch, having some differences of no small consequence
with Charles the most serene Prince
of Castile, sent me into Flanders, as his ambassador,
for treating and composing matters between them.

text: I would, according to the proverb, “Show the sun with a lantern.
chunks: I would,
according to the proverb,
“Show the sun
with a lantern.

text: Those that were appointed by the Prince to treat with us, met us at Bruges, according to agreement; they were all worthy men.
zh: 根据协议，王子任命的那些与我们会面的人在布鲁日与我们会面。他们都是有价值的人。
chunks: Those that were appointed by the Prince
to treat with us,
met us at Bruges,
according to agreement;
they were all worthy men.

text: Provost of Casselsee: both art and nature had concurred to make him eloquent: he was very learned in the law; and, as he had a great capacity, so, by a long practice in affairs, he was very dexterous at unravelling them.
zh: 卡塞尔湖教务长：艺术与自然的结合使他能言善辩：他在法律方面很有学识；由于他能力很强，经过长期的实践，他能够非常灵巧地解决这些问题。
chunks: Provost of Casselsee: both art and nature had concurred to make him eloquent:
he was very learned in the law; and,
as he had a great capacity, so,
by a long practice in affairs,
he was very dexterous at unravelling them.

text: After we had several times met, without coming to an agreement, they went to Brussels for some days, to know the Prince’s pleasure; and, since our business would admit it, I went to Antwerp.
zh: 我们见过几次面，但没有达成协议，他们就去布鲁塞尔待了几天，想知道王子的喜好。而且，既然我们的生意承认这一点，我就去了安特卫普。
chunks: After we had several times met,
without coming to an agreement,
they went to Brussels for some days,
to know the Prince’s pleasure; and,
since our business would admit it, I went to Antwerp.

text: His conversation was so pleasant and so innocently cheerful, that his company in a great measure lessened any longings to go back to my country, and to my wife and children, which an absence of four months had quickened very much.
zh: 他的谈话是如此愉快，如此天真快乐，他的陪伴在很大程度上减少了我想回到我的国家、我的妻子和孩子身边的渴望，而四个月的缺席已经大大加快了这种渴望。
chunks: His conversation was so pleasant and so innocently cheerful, that his company
in a great measure lessened any longings
to go back to my country,
and to my wife and children, which an absence
of four months had quickened very much.

text: Peter saw me, he came and saluted me, and as I was returning his civility, he took me aside, and pointing to him with whom he had been discoursing, he said, “Do you see that man?
zh: 彼得看见我，走过来向我打招呼，当我回敬他的客气时，他把我拉到一边，指着刚才与他谈话的那个人说：“你看到那个人了吗？
chunks: Peter saw me, he came and saluted me,
and as I was returning his civility,
he took me aside, and pointing to him
with whom he had been discoursing,
he said, “Do you see that man?

text: I was just thinking to bring him to you.
zh: 我只是想带他来见你。
chunks: I was just thinking
to bring him to you.

text: I answered, “He should have been very welcome on your account.
zh: 我回答说：“你应该非常欢迎他。
chunks: I answered,
“He should have been very welcome
on your account.

text: And on his own too,” replied he, “if you knew the man, for there is none alive that can give so copious an account of unknown nations and countries as he can do, which I know you very much desire.
chunks: And on his own too, ” replied he,
“if you knew the man, for there is none alive
that can give so copious an account
of unknown nations and countries as he can do,
which I know you very much desire.

text: Then,” said I, “I did not guess amiss, for at first sight I took him for a seaman.
zh: 那么，”我说，“我没有猜错，因为第一眼看到他时我以为他是个海员。
chunks: Then,
” said I,
“I did not guess amiss,
for at first sight I took him
for a seaman.

text: But you are much mistaken,” said he, “for he has not sailed as a seaman, but as a traveller, or rather a philosopher.
zh: 但你就大错特错了，”他说，“因为他并不是以海员的身份出航，而是以旅行者的身份，或者更确切地说，以哲学家的身份出航。
chunks: But you are much mistaken,
” said he,
“for he has not sailed
as a seaman, but as a traveller,
or rather a philosopher.

text: The leaving him thus did not a little gratify one that was more fond of travelling than of returning home to be buried in his own country; for he used often to say, that the way to heaven was the same from all places, and he that had no grave had the heavens still over him.
chunks: The leaving him thus did not a little gratify one
that was more fond of travelling than of returning home to be buried
in his own country; for he used often
to say, that the way to heaven was the same from all places, and he

text: After those civilities were past which are usual with strangers upon their first meeting, we all went to my house, and entering into the garden, sat down on a green bank and entertained one another in discourse.
zh: 过了陌生人初次见面时常见的礼节后，我们都到了我家，走进花园，坐在绿色的岸边，互相交谈。
chunks: After those civilities were past which are usual with strangers
upon their first meeting, we all went
to my house, and entering
into the garden, sat down on a green bank
and entertained one another in discourse.

text: There they found the conveniencies of seeing many countries on all hands, for no ship went any voyage into which he and his companions were not very welcome.
zh: 在那里，他们发现了游览许多国家的便利，因为没有一艘船去任何他和他的同伴不受欢迎的航程。
chunks: There they found the conveniencies
of seeing many countries on all hands,
for no ship went any voyage
into which he
and his companions were not very welcome.

text: The first vessels that they saw were flat-bottomed, their sails were made of reeds and wicker, woven close together, only some were of leather; but, afterwards, they found ships made with round keels and canvas sails, and in all respects like our ships, and the seamen understood both astronomy and navigation.

text: He got wonderfully into their favour by showing them the use of the needle, of which till then they were utterly ignorant.
zh: 他向他们展示了针的使用方法，奇妙地赢得了他们的青睐，而在此之前他们对此一无所知。

into their favour
by showing them the use
of the needle,
of which till then they were utterly ignorant.

text: We asked him many questions concerning all these things, to which he answered very willingly; we made no inquiries after monsters, than which nothing is more common; for everywhere one may hear of ravenous dogs and wolves, and cruel men-eaters, but it is not so easy to find states that are well and wisely governed.

text: I think my friends ought to rest contented with this, and not to expect that for their sakes I should enslave myself to any king whatsoever.

to rest contented
with this, and not to expect

zh: 温柔又公平！”彼得说； “我并不是说你应该成为任何国王的奴隶，而是说你应该协助他们，对他们有用。
chunks: Soft and fair!” said Peter; “I do not mean
that you should be a slave
to any king, but only
that you should assist them
and be useful to them.

text: The change of the word,” said he, “does not alter the matter.

chunks: The change
of the word,
” said he,
“does not alter the matter.

zh: 但随你怎么说吧，”彼得回答说，“我看不出还有什么其他方式可以使你如此有用，无论是在私下里对你的朋友还是在公众面前，而且你可以使自己的处境更幸福。
chunks: But term it as you will, ” replied Peter,
“I do not see any other way in which you can be
so useful, both in private to your friends
and to the public, and by
which you can make your own condition happier.

text: Raphael, “is that to be compassed in a way so abhorrent to my genius?

to be compassed
in a way
so abhorrent
to my genius?

text: Now I live as I will, to which I believe, few courtiers can pretend; and there are so many that court the favour of great men, that there will be no great loss if they are not troubled either with me or with others of my temper.
zh: 现在我按照自己的意愿生活，我相信很少有朝臣能够假装做到这一点；有这么多人讨好伟人的青睐，如果他们不为我或与我脾气相同的人烦恼，也不会有什么大损失。
